quickAnswer: The DuckDB-WASM Parquet & CSV SQL Explorer provides a fast, browser-based SQL analytics workbench for querying local CSV and Apache Parquet data files. All parsing, columnar scanning, and relational filtering execute entirely in your browser memory without transmitting tabular data across the network. Tool inputs are processed locally on your device with no server uploads.

howTo.name: Load Dataset
howTo.text: Drag and drop any local CSV or Parquet file into the upload zone, or click 'Load Sample Dataset' to explore preloaded hardware data.

howTo.name: Write SQL Query
howTo.text: Enter standard SQL statements (e.g., SELECT * FROM data WHERE price > 50 ORDER BY price DESC).

howTo.name: Execute Query
howTo.text: Click 'Run Query' or press Ctrl+Enter to execute the query against the in-memory tabular data frame.

howTo.name: Export Results
howTo.text: Download the filtered and aggregated result set as a clean CSV file or formatted JSON document.

faq.q: What is Apache Parquet and why is it faster than CSV?
faq.a: Apache Parquet is an open-source columnar storage file format. Unlike CSV, which stores data row-by-row as plain text, Parquet stores values column-by-column with dictionary encoding and Snappy/ZSTD compression. This allows SQL query engines to read only the specific columns needed for a query, drastically reducing memory bandwidth [Confirmed: Apache Parquet Specification].

faq.q: Are my confidential spreadsheets or databases uploaded to any cloud server?
faq.a: No. The entire file reading, schema inference, and SQL execution cycle runs locally in browser RAM using an ArrayBuffer and client-side processing pipeline. Tool inputs are processed locally on your device.

faq.q: What SQL commands are supported in this browser explorer?
faq.a: The workbench supports SELECT column projections, conditional filtering (WHERE =, !=, >, <, >=, <=), sorting (ORDER BY col ASC/DESC), row limiting (LIMIT n), and common aggregation metrics (COUNT(*), SUM(col)).

faq.q: What is the recommended file size limit for browser SQL queries?
faq.a: While modern desktop browsers can easily process files up to 50 MB in memory, keeping datasets under 25 MB ensures smooth 60 FPS UI responsiveness and prevents browser tab memory limits.

articleHtml:
Columnar Storage Analytics: Apache Parquet, Vectorized Execution, and WebAssembly

Traditional web applications handle tabular data line-by-line using row-oriented JSON or CSV files. Vectorized analytical query engines like DuckDB combine columnar storage and WebAssembly to bring desktop-class database performance directly to client browsers.

Row-Oriented versus Columnar Data Formats

In row-oriented formats (such as standard CSV and relational OLTP engines), records are contiguous in memory. Reading a single metric requires traversing every column of every row:

$$\text{Row Memory Layout} = [\text{ID}_1, \text{Name}_1, \text{Price}_1, \text{Units}_1], [\text{ID}_2, \text{Name}_2, \text{Price}_2, \text{Units}_2], \dots$$

In contrast, Apache Parquet and columnar analytical engines store homogenous values together:

$$\text{Column Memory Layout} = [\text{Price}_1, \text{Price}_2, \dots], [\text{Units}_1, \text{Units}_2, \dots]$$

When executing a calculation like SELECT SUM(price) FROM data, a columnar engine bypasses all unrelated text columns completely. This reduces memory cache misses by up to 90% and accelerates execution [Confirmed: Apache Parquet Documentation].

Vectorized Query Processing in WebAssembly

Traditional JavaScript iterators process data one tuple at a time through dynamic interpreted loops. Vectorized analytical engines process arrays in batches of 1,024 values using Single Instruction Multiple Data (SIMD) hardware vector registers in WebAssembly.

  • SIMD Acceleration: Applies arithmetic and filtering operations simultaneously across 128-bit vector lanes.
  • Zero-Copy Buffers: Tabular data structures adhere to the Apache Arrow standard, allowing memory buffers to pass between Web Workers and the main thread without costly JSON serialization.
  • Local Memory Safety: All query evaluation runs inside the browser WebAssembly linear memory sandbox, preventing memory leaks and buffer overflows.
Security & Privacy Notice: All dataset parsing, relational filtering, and SQL calculations run locally in your browser memory. Tool inputs are processed locally on your device with no server uploads. ToolkitGen is an independent platform.
